name: Jagsonpal Pharmaceuticals Ltd
title: Jagsonpal Pharmaceuticals Ltd - 507789 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue up 9.3% to Rs81 crore with Aequitas and Group Pharma acquisitions adding consolidated Rs96 crore; organic growth still short of the 1.5x IPM target, so the Q3 pivot is unproven.

summary.headline: Jagsonpal Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 9.3% YoY to INR81 crores, with H1 organic growth at 9.3% and management targeting INR100 crores quarterly revenue in Q3.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first quarter with Aequitas consolidated and included the Group Pharma wellness brands from 1 October. Standalone revenue grew 9.3% YoY to INR81 crores and consolidated revenue reached INR96 crores (up 29%). Standalone EBITDA margin was 22.7% and consolidated 19.3%, with H1 EBITDA margin at 22.9%, up 40 bps. Management reiterated the INR500 crore revenue vision for FY28 on an organic basis, but admitted growth remains short of expectations and is still below the IPM rate.

financial_highlights.change: H1 64.7%, up close to 70 bps YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated net operating cash flow (H1 FY27)

segments.name: Standalone branded business (Jagsonpal)
segments.commentary: Q2 growth around 15% vs IPM ~12% in Jul-Sep 2026; H1 around 15% vs IPM ~11%. Branded prescription growing over 10%, contributing around 11-11.5% of growth. Top 10 brands are about 58% of revenue, nine ranked top 5 in their markets.

segments.name: Aequitas Healthcare (hospital and critical care, acquired July 2026)
segments.commentary: First full quarter consolidated; provides entry into corporate hospital chains, which management says now contribute over 11.5% of industry sales. Dedicated business head appointed; first value-added launch targeted for end-November with go-to-market in early December. Hospital margins are structurally lower.

segments.name: Group Pharma wellness portfolio (acquired October 2026)
segments.commentary: Two established brands (hematinics and respiratory) sold in 6 states, adding around 10,000 doctors and an approximate INR1.75 crore base. Management says margins are similar to Jagsonpal; cross-selling planned in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka.

guidance_outlook: Quarterly revenue to cross INR100 crores in Q3 FY27; management said Q3 growth would be above 1.5x IPM and EBITDA-accretive.
INR500 crore revenue vision by FY28 (calendar 2028), organic only, excluding further acquisitions; management says it is aspirational but has a road map.
Blended consolidated EBITDA margin expected to return to around 22% or more; Q3 said to be above 22% and Q4 seasonally weaker.
Standalone gross margin expected to improve 50-75 bps YoY; consolidated gross margin to stay near Q2 level. Aequitas benefits from procurement and supply-chain actions expected only from Q4.
Full-year Aequitas revenue guidance of INR100 crores by FY28 unchanged. No new product launches planned in Q3 beyond the Aequitas brand; some launches planned for Q4.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model; no manufacturing capacity disclosed. Management says no manpower addition beyond budgeted numbers.
Investment in people: MR productivity up about 10%, hospital team being built to cross-sell into Aequitas network.
Management is evaluating whether to own backend (API or formulation) manufacturing for future expansion outside India; no decision yet, with the company citing ample capital flexibility.
demand_pricing: Gynaecology is the largest contributor (about 35,000 gynaecologists engaged), followed by orthopaedics and dermatology.
Maintane grew around 29% in Q2 vs molecule ~20%; Metadec ~14% vs ~13%; Lycored ~15% vs ~13%; Endoreg ~20% vs market degrowth.
Indocap grew 4.5%, about 1% below its market; Equirex is constrained by NRx restrictions. Management expects a packaging and indication innovation for Indocap in November.
Hospital contract pricing is under pressure from API price declines over the last 12 months; contracts are typically annual.
New products contributed about 2.3-2.5% of growth; in-licensing talks on 1-2 opportunities are ongoing but margins expected to be low.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR500 crore by FY28 realistic given about 10% growth and a INR75 crore acquired run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it aspirational but based on organic growth with a clear road map and no further acquisitions; it cites multiple investments in launches and people, and a growth acceleration expected from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company provide a separate organic vs inorganic growth line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the split will be given as commentary, not a separate line. Group Pharma's contribution will be measured against the 6 states it covers, with its base around INR1.75 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Aequitas and Group Pharma rather than deepen gynae and derma?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said few gynae or ortho targets were available or affordable. Aequitas gives hospital channel access; Group Pharma offers a culturally similar organisation, distribution in 6 states, and co-prescription brands with similar margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone gross margin is close to 65% and expected to rise 50-75 bps YoY; the Aequitas hospital business is lower margin, so consolidated margin should stay close to Q2 levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Pharmarack IPM figure ahead of reported growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the data is sample-based and differs from internal numbers; internal branded prescription growth is over 10%, and the gap is expected to narrow in a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any issues with ramping up the Aequitas portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ramp-up is on plan, with API-driven price pressure in hospital contracts; procurement benefits are expected to start from Q4, and full-year Aequitas revenue guidance of INR100 crores by FY28 is unchanged.

risks_watch: Organic growth of 9.3% in H1 is below the 1.5x IPM target and below management's own expectations; Q3 must show the promised acceleration.
Consolidated EBITDA margin of 19.3% against the 22% target depends on Aequitas margin improvement, which management expects only from Q4.
Pharmarack IPM data (12-16.8%) runs ahead of reported growth; management attributes this to sampling and secondary stocking, and the gap needs to close.
Hospital channel pricing pressure from API cost increases and annual contracts.
Strategic direction beyond FY28 remains undecided, including possible backend or manufacturing investment and the chronic-therapy shift, with the discussion still with promoters and the board.
Indocap (legacy brand) growing below market; Equirex constrained by NRx regulation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term vision and acquisition integration, but openly cautious on current organic growth, which management repeatedly called lower than its own expectations. Answers were more specific on the Q3 timelines than on longer-term plans, which management declined to detail.
key_quotes: Q3 will definitely deliver more than 22%. It's generally Q4, which is a bit of a drag in India, which pulls down the margin.
These are critical care products you can't do much about. So nothing has been a surprise.
So it's a pure organic growth that will lead to these numbers over next 2 years, nothing beyond that.

growth.why: Management guides standalone quarterly revenue above INR100 crore in Q3 FY27 (vs INR81 crore in Q2, implying a step-up) and 1.5x IPM growth, backed partly by the Group Pharma brands, Aequitas and Maintane/Endoreg momentum, but no specific capacity or order book was disclosed, and the INR500 crore FY28 vision is admitted as aspirational.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone gross margin guided up 50-75 bps YoY from 64.1% in Q2, and consolidated EBITDA margin guided back to 22%+ (vs 19.3% in Q2), though Aequitas procurement benefits start only from Q4 and Q4 is seasonally weaker.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Asset-light model with no manufacturing capacity disclosed and no manpower addition beyond budget; backend manufacturing is under evaluation with no decision yet.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides standalone quarterly revenue above INR100 crore in Q3 (vs INR81 crore in Q2, a ~23% step-up) and growth above 1.5x IPM (IPM ~12% in Q2), though H1 organic growth is only 9.3%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is asset-light, has disclosed no capacity and utilisation is not discussed; backend manufacturing for overseas expansion is undecided, so no capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious on current organic growth (9.3% H1 vs IPM ~11%) and called it below its own expectations; guidance was held, not raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 must deliver the INR100 crore quarter and 1.5x IPM growth from a 9.3% H1 base; the consolidated 22% margin depends on Aequitas improvement that only starts in Q4.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aequitas first value-added launch targeted for end-November with go-to-market in early December, and some Q4 launches are planned, though no new launches are planned in Q3 beyond Aequitas and new products are only 2.3-2.5% of growth.

rows.label: Group Pharma wellness cross-selling in MP, UP, Karnataka
rows.why: Group Pharma adds about 10,000 doctors and an approximate INR1.75 crore base across 6 states, with cross-selling planned in three states, but the size of the lift is not quantified.

rows.label: Hospital contract pricing pressure from API cost declines
rows.why: Hospital contracts are annual and under price pressure from API price declines over the last 12 months, which weighs on Aequitas margins that are structurally lower.

rows.label: Aequitas procurement and supply-chain savings
rows.why: Management expects procurement and supply-chain actions to lift Aequitas margins only from Q4, which is needed to bring consolidated EBITDA margin from 19.3% back to 22%+.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR500 crore FY28 vision, Q3 INR100 crore revenue and acquisition integration, but openly cautious that organic growth (9.3% H1) is below IPM and its own expectations. Analysts pressed on the feasibility of INR500 crore on about 10% growth and the gap between IPM data
